title: Build a reconciled portfolio ledger

objectives.text: Implement a bounded two-instrument confirmed-fill replay with identity-aware duplicate policy, signed cash/positions, marks and explicit economic-accounting boundaries.
Reconcile cash/positions independently, test replay/failure/valuation invariants and preserve unexplained breaks instead of fabricating balancing events or settled/tradable balances.

blocks.markdown: Build a complete small ledger for one synthetic account/currency, instruments A and B, flat initial positions and stated initial cash. Events are already-confirmed fills with globally unique execution IDs WITHIN this declared account/source namespace. A/B are synthetic identities, not real tickers. Record signed integer shares, positive integer price cents/share and nonnegative per-fill fee cents. Marks are positive integer cents for exactly A and B under a separately verified valuation policy. No orders, FX, tax, income, financing, corporate actions, settlement timing or credit permissions are modeled.

The input list is the complete authoritative replay sequence. A repeated ID with identical payload is an explicit no-op counted as duplicate; a repeated ID with changed payload raises ValueError as a conflict. This is a toy immutable-execution policy, NOT a universal broker correction/bust protocol. A real correction needs its own authenticated event/version rules. Different sources/accounts may reuse IDs, so their namespaces cannot be silently merged. Preserve originals and report conflicts rather than overwriting them as latest truth.

Start q_A = q_B = 0 and cash=C0. For every first-seen fill, update only its symbol's position by Δq and cash by -Δq*p-fee. Therefore final cash = C0-sum_unique(Δq*p+fee) and each position equals that symbol's unique signed-fill sum. Marked equity=cash+sum_s q_s*m_s, net marked PnL = equity-C0 under the no-other-flows scope. Changing marks alone must not change cash/position/fees; its equity effect is sum q_s*Δm_s. This capstone reports total marked PnL, not a new realized/tax-basis decomposition.

blocks.title: Two instruments share cash, not price units or identities

steps.text: Start cash 100000 cents. Buy 10 A at 1000 with fee 2: cash 89998, A 10. Buy 4 B at 2000 with fee 3: cash 81995, B 4.
Sell 3 A at 1100 with fee 1 adds 3299 cash: final 85294, A 7, B 4, total fees 6. Repeating the exact E1 must not debit another 10002 or add another 10 shares.
Marks A 1050 and B 1900 give position value 7350+7600 = 14950, equity 100244 and net PnL 244.
An independent statement reporting cash 85296 has a 2 cent break. Do not add a fake 2 cent rebate merely to make the report match. Check completeness, fees, scope and timing against source evidence.

blocks.caption: Expected result: cash 85294, positions A 7/B 4, fees 6, equity 100244, net_pnl 244, applied 3, duplicates 1; then conflicting duplicate rejected. The function computes into local state and publishes no partial result if validation/conflict raises. It does not mutate event/mark inputs, write a database, authenticate events or prove crash-safe atomic commit; those are later service responsibilities.

blocks.markdown: Compare the replay result with an independently sourced statement/snapshot on matching account/instrument/currency/as-of and trade-date versus settled scope. Breaks are statement-minus-ledger by the declared sign convention. Check cash separately from each position: offsetting wrong instruments can hide in one total. Internal identities can pass when an event is consistently missing from every local calculation. A duplicate policy can also hide a genuinely different trade if identity binding is wrong, so uniqueness/source provenance is load-bearing.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 0; {'A': 0, 'B': 0}; 2; True. The reference statement matches cash/positions first. Adding a deliberate 2 cents to statement cash then exposes a 2 cent break. Repeating the exact full batch leaves cash unchanged. The local raw-fill sum checks implementation arithmetic; a truly independent statement is still needed to detect source omissions. No discrepancy is silently repaired.

blocks.markdown: Required tests: empty valid log, each side/symbol, multiple prices/fees, exact repeated IDs, conflicting IDs, bad symbols/types/ranges, source immutability and replay from the same complete input. Because this function has no external state and raises before returning on a later invalid event, the caller gets no new committed snapshot on failure; this is not durable transaction/rollback proof. If adapting to persistence, stage/validate first and commit atomically with event/version identity and recovery tests instead of treating local exceptions as database guarantees.

A mark is a valuation input, not proof of available liquidation liquidity. Short/negative-cash states can appear mathematically and require actual margin/borrow/funding rules before any trading interpretation. A fully replayed ledger can still differ from a settled-cash/custody report because of legitimate timing or omitted modeled event categories; diagnose scope before calling either side wrong. Settled cash, order exposure and economic inventory are separate. No result creates a live order, authorizes a transfer or establishes professional competence.

Independent transfer: add a read-only per-event audit trace, preserving duplicate/conflict semantics and immutable inputs. Reconcile each instrument and cash against a separately constructed reference. Test mark-only changes, duplicated full batch and one conflicting reused ID late in the log; verify no partial snapshot is returned or input changed. Then list the new event/schema/identity rules required before supporting a dividend, stock split, FX conversion or corrected trade rather than improvising a balancing cash adjustment.

References: [FINRA confirmation/source reconciliation](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/checking-trade-confirmations), [broker accounting-convention dependence](https://ibkrguides.com/reportingreference/reportguide/realized_unrealizedperformancesummary_default.htm), and [DTCC eligible clearing/settlement distinction](https://www.dtcc.com/products-and-services/clearing-settlement-services/equities-clearing/cns). The two-symbol identity/duplicate/fee rules are explicitly synthetic implementation contracts, not attributed to a real broker, statement format or settlement system.

summary: A replayed portfolio ledger needs source-bound execution identity, exact per-instrument/cash invariants and independent reconciliation. Duplicate handling, local failure behavior and marks have declared scope; none proves settled balances, durable service safety or trading authority.
